clue.text: Horse with wind knocked over old duke's pompadour?

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
air is moving wind, as in a breath of air

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue means the following pair of letters is turned upside down, read backwards

explanation.surface: A horse is winded after toppling an aged duke wearing a fancy hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns OD into DO. The question mark flags that a pompadour is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a swept-up hairstyle, an example of a styled coiffure.

clue.text: If really necessary, chap will get drunk with a tin

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A man will get tipsy if he really must, given a can of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges CHAP and A TIN together; 'will get' and 'with' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for doing something only in an emergency is to do it if really necessary.

clue.text: PM inhales dope with Hoskins here and there in Rome

indicators.note: something that inhales takes material inside itself, so the other letters go within these

parts.note: PM is taken as written, the Prime Minister
a dope is a fool, an ass
the setter Hoskins refers to himself, giving I

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister smokes cannabis alongside the setter at various spots in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' tells you the definition is a Latin word, used in English for references scattered through a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim is Latin for scattered throughout, used by scholars for references occurring here and there.

clue.text: Former Brazilian player sending down large strip

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a letter down moves it lower in the word, here to the end

parts.note: Pelé was the great Brazilian footballer
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A retired Brazilian footballer is sent off, wearing a big shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending down' moves the L of PELE to the bottom, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip off the skin or a layer is to peel it.

clue.text: Detectives offer to take in radical US prisoner

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police detectives

indicators.note: to take in means to enclose, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at auction
R is an abbreviation for radical, as in political labels

explanation.surface: Police detectives make a deal to bring in an American extremist convict.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardbird is American slang for a convict, someone confined to a prison yard.

clue.text: A record broken by half-cut sleuth in bed, perhaps

indicators.note: something broken by another piece is split open with that piece inserted

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A record is interrupted by a drunken detective, perhaps passed out in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' reads as drunk in the surface, but here it means keeping just the first half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is typically found in bed, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Cloudy and no blue about? You close to Inverness?

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: close to means the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: The sky is overcast with no blue around, as you'd expect near Inverness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NO BLUE into NEBULO; Inverness is in rainy Scotland, so the surface is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulous means hazy or vague, like a nebula or cloud.

clue.text: At peace, travelling round southern tip of NZ

indicators.note: round means going around, so these letters enclose the other piece
travelling means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Calm while journeying round the bottom end of New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' gives EATCAPE, and 'round' makes it enclose the S. East Cape is in the North Island, so 'tip' is not the southern end.
explanation.definitionFit: East Cape is the easternmost point of New Zealand's North Island, a geographical tip.

clue.text: Gold bag brought over containing small pen

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: brought over means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to net is to bag or catch

explanation.surface: A gold bag, carried across, holds a little pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is a writer by metonymy, not the stationery item.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen was a novelist, and a writer can be called a pen.

clue.text: Like some comfy shoes creep doles out?

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wondering phrase about whether a sneaky person hands out comfortable footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CREEP and DOLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe-soled shoes have soft crinkled rubber soles, a cushioned and comfortable footwear style.

clue.text: Some characters involved in college tuition case

indicators.note: some characters within a phrase means a run of its letters lies inside it

explanation.surface: Part of the fees for a college course involves a legal dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Issue with old lady getting with new boyfriend

parts.note: issue means offspring, a person's young
old lady is slang for mother, MA

explanation.surface: A problem arises when Mum takes up with a new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem but means children.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's young man is her romantic partner or suitor.

clue.text: Turning 100, Catholic husband becomes sex symbol!

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a ton is a hundred

explanation.surface: A Catholic husband reaching a hundred becomes a heart-throb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses TON. The definition is a cheeky one: a notch on a bedpost marks a sexual conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch carved on the bedpost is the traditional tally mark for a sexual conquest.

clue.text: Taking drug, get better for unrehearsed performance

indicators.note: taking means removing, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: to improve is to get better
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone uses drugs to recover for an off-the-cuff show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking drug' looks like consuming it, but here it takes E out.
explanation.definitionFit: Improv is short for improvisation, comedy or theatre made up on the spot.

clue.text: Vacuous accountant described by my swearword

indicators.note: described by means encircled, so the outer piece is drawn around the other

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, as is oh

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: An empty-headed accountant is described with a curse word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacuous' empties the word of everything but its ends; 'described by' means drawn around, and 'my!' is an exclamation like 'oh!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a profanity or curse, not only a solemn promise.

clue.text: A rogue record label first to attack the scholarly world

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue
EMI is a well-known British record label

indicators.note: first to means the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A rogue record company leads the charge against universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the community and environment of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Tough youth seen behind a conservative faked it

indicators.note: seen behind means this piece comes after the others

parts.note: a Ted is a Teddy boy, a 1950s British tough

explanation.surface: A young thug spotted behind a Tory was only pretending.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress with a rough reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to pretend or put on a show, so someone who acted was faking.

clue.text: Awful chatter hindering a vicar doing wedding vows?

indicators.note: hindering means getting in the way, so the other piece is lodged inside
awful means bad or messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dreadful gossip gets in the way of a clergyman conducting a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges CHATTER, and A goes inside. The question mark marks a whimsical definition: one who ties the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar marrying a couple joins them together, so he is literally an attacher.

clue.text: Leaders in America rightly slam enraged Trump?

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Leaders in America are right to criticise an angry Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a trump is a fart, which comes from the backside; the surface invites the political reading too.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump is British slang for breaking wind, which issues from the backside, giving a playful link.

clue.text: Passage I'll consider carefully from an audiobook

indicators.note: an audiobook is heard rather than read, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: to weigh is to consider carefully, so this phrase gives I'll weigh

explanation.surface: Someone promises to ponder a stretch of text heard on an audiobook.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL WEIGH, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisleway is a walkway between seats or shelves, a passage.

clue.text: Joint a male found by marijuana container

parts.note: a J is slang for a cannabis joint
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A man is found with a joint and some cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found by' just places pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A jampot is a pot that holds jam, a kitchen container.

clue.text: Occasion Her Maj will avoid one giving out lines

indicators.note: to avoid means to leave out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: a prompter feeds actors their forgotten lines
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen will stay away from a theatre prompt at a big event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasion' is a verb here, meaning to cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To occasion something is to cause or bring it about, which is to prompt it.

clue.text: In a state of agitation, he struck pushy salesman

indicators.note: agitation means stirring up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Worked up, he hit an aggressive salesperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state of agitation' rearranges HE STRUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A huckster is a hawker who sells aggressively or dishonestly.

clue.text: Tory with nothing on beginning to bother rabbit

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
FA is short for 'sweet Fanny Adams', British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A naked Conservative starts to pester a bunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is British rhyming slang (rabbit and pork, talk) for chatter, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A confab is a chat, and to rabbit means to chatter on.

clue.text: Going around Iranian capital and church is a treat!

indicators.note: going around means turning back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the rial is Iran's currency, its capital in the money sense
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Touring around Tehran and a church makes for a lovely outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iranian capital' tempts you to Tehran, but means money: the rial.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a cream-filled pastry, a sweet indulgence.

clue.text: Protest Hoskins making comeback in work

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: to do is to work or perform

indicators.note: making a comeback means returning, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter Hoskins refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter protests about making a return to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns ME into EM, placed 'in' DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for demonstration, a public protest.

clue.text: See you said outlaw dogs? But they can give you a lift!

definitions.text: they can give you a lift!

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the letters stand for how the words sound

parts.note: see you sounds like the letters C and U
to outlaw is to ban
to dog someone is to follow at their heels, so dogs are heels

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye and bans dogs, yet these can lift your spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they can give you a lift' plays on raising your height.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuban heels are thick, moderately high shoe heels that add height.

clue.text: Live without sex? That's something to chew on!

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
it is a euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: Can you live without sex? That's food for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite is a mouthful of food, literally something to chew.

clue.text: Egyptian banker stealing pennies is bit of a tit

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the other piece is held inside

parts.note: the Nile is Egypt's river, something with banks
P is the abbreviation for penny, so two pennies are PP

explanation.surface: An Egyptian bank worker pocketing small change is a bit of a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a river (it has banks), and 'tit' is a breast, not a fool or bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A nipple is the small projection at the tip of a breast.

clue.text: Booze time? Hoskins is getting a flipping excellent drop of red

parts.note: the setter Hoskins speaking of himself would say I am

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI

indicators.note: a drop of means just the first letter

explanation.surface: Drinks time: the setter is enjoying a bloody good drop of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild curse but reverses AIR (A1 read as AI, plus R) into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a coffee liqueur, an alcoholic drink.
